📊 August 2026 Northern Colorado Market Update — Late-Summer Edition

Our team just published the latest breakdown of home prices, inventory, and trends across Northern Colorado. Here's what we're seeing:

🏘️ Fort Collins — median single-family ~$610K, steady through July with inventory up ~15% year-over-year. Days on market averaging 40 days; homes priced right in the $500K-$650K range still attract offers within three weeks.

🌲 Loveland — the region's most balanced market at ~$510K median (+3.6% YoY). Inventory up 14%, and first-time buyer activity remains strong with CHFA down payment assistance.

🏠 Windsor — premium pricing at ~$588K median. Sellers are now receiving ~97.8% of list price on average, down from 99% a year ago. The $450K-$600K segment stays active while upper-tier homes need realistic pricing.

🌄 Greeley — Northern Colorado's affordability anchor at ~$432K median. Move-in-ready homes under $400K are the fastest-moving segment in the region, often under contract in 10-14 days.

🚧 Growth corridor: Timnath ~$650K (inventory up 20% YoY) and Severance ~$525K continue to attract buyers seeking newer homes and more land.

Key takeaway: The most buyer-friendly market since early 2022 — more inventory, steady rates in the mid-6% to low-7% range, and sellers offering concessions. But well-priced homes still move quickly.

Full blog with city-by-city analysis ⟶ https://saahomes.com/blog/northern-colorado-market-update-august-2026/
